request.message: Why can duplicate generation corrupt both answer quality and proof integrity in an asynchronous cognitive service? Compare an early single-owner design with a late deduplication design, then choose the stronger architecture and explain how you would verify it under cancellation, timeout, and worker-restart faults.

response.response: <div class="" response of request> Duplicate't answer quality and proof integrity in an asynchronous cognitive service. Compare early single-owner design with late deduplication design, then choose the stronger architecture and explain how you would verify it under cancellation, timeout, and worker-restart faults. </request <response> In an asynchronous cognitive service where requests can trigger multiple concurrent processing threads due to race conditions or retries, duplicate generation refers to redundant computation of the same request. This redundancy affects answer quality and proof integrity in several ways: 1. **Answer Quality**: If duplicates produce different results (due to non-determinism), aggregating these responses without coordination leads to inconsistent answers. 2. **Proof Integrity**: Proofs generated by each thread need to be consistent with one another; otherwise, verification fails or becomes extremely complex. ### Early Single-Owner Design This approach assigns ownership of a request ID early in the processing pipeline — ideally at ingress. The first worker that acquires an exclusive lock on this request is designated as "owner" and proceeds while others are blocked or discarded. Pros: - Simple locking mechanism ensures only one thread computes per unique request, preserving quality & integrity easily. Cons: - Lock contention can become bottleneck under high concurrency - Deadlocks may occur if locks aren't released promptly ### Late Deduplication Design This approach allows all threads to compute concurrently but deduplicates results post-computation based on some deterministic criteria (e.g., timestamp of completion). Pros: - Higher throughput as no upfront locking needed, better for highly concurrent loads.
